Test uses a single typical array length and a typical index (3). There are no checks of boundary inputs (index 0, last index, negative values, empty arrays), so boundary conditions are not examined.

The test is short and self-contained (no repeated blocks within class fragment). There are no visible duplicated setup blocks in this single-method class; its brevity and lack of repetition meet the rule for modular short tests.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The method is short (< 20 lines) and linear, with no loops or conditionals; cyclomatic complexity is low, satisfying the size and simplicity criteria.

The test contains a single superficial assertion (assertEquals on length) and does not verify multiple properties of the result (e.g., contents, order). This provides limited fault-detection capability.
There are no @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out @Test methods in the visible code; the test is active and runnable.
No annotations or Javadoc link the test to a requirement, ticket, or user story (no @Story, @Requirement, or REQ- IDs), so traceability is absent.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The test class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class) at the class level, providing categorization useful for selective execution.

PRINCIPLE: Each test should focus on a single requirement/behavior with one clear Arrange-Act-Assert. RATIONALE: Single-focus tests make root causes easier to identify. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant tests contain exactly one method call being tested and one assertion group. DECISION RULES: 1) Count distinct Act operations: the method performs a single constructor call (one Act). 2) Check for presence of a clear Assert block: none present. 3) If only one method call AND one assertion group -> compliant. There is no assertion, so the test lacks an explicit Assert phase and does not clearly specify the expected behavior. VERDICT: non-compliant because the test only constructs an object without asserting expected outcomes or behaviors.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must not depend on execution order or shared mutable state. RATIONALE: Independence enables parallel and order-insensitive execution. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Presence of @Before/@After or tests using only local variables. DECISION RULES: 1) Check for @Before/@After in method: none required. 2) Check for shared mutable state: method uses only a local variable. 3) If tests use only local variables, mark compliant. VERDICT: compliant because the test uses only a local variable and does not modify shared or static state.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Provide tests for both happy path and error cases. RATIONALE: Ensures robustness and correct handling of invalid inputs or exceptions. EVALUATION CRITERIA: For each method being tested, there should be at least one happy-path test and one error scenario test (e.g., @Test(expected=...) or assertThrows). DECISION RULES: 1) Count test methods covering the subject: the class contains a single simple test (only happy path-like construction). 2) No tests for exceptional conditions are present. 3) If class has <2 test methods or lacks exception tests, mark non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because there is a single test that only constructs the object and no test exercising error/exceptional flows.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should validate min/max and just-outside-boundary values. RATIONALE: Boundaries are common sources of bugs. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for empty strings, zero, negative numbers, Integer.MAX_VALUE, etc. DECISION RULES: If the method under test doesn't take inputs with obvious numeric/string boundaries (e.g., a no-arg constructor), mark not-applicable. VERDICT: not-applicable because the test only invokes a no-argument constructor and there are no input boundaries to exercise in this method.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be self-contained and reuse helper methods for duplicated logic. RATIONALE: Reduces duplication and improves maintainability. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Presence of helper methods or constants; if tests are very short and do not repeat code they're acceptable. DECISION RULES: 1) Look for helper methods/constants: none required. 2) If tests are very short (<10 lines) and don't repeat code, mark compliant. VERDICT: compliant because the single test is very short and does not exhibit duplication within the class.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Keep test methods small and with low cyclomatic complexity. RATIONALE: Simpler tests are easier to inspect and maintain. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Tests <20 lines and no loops/complex conditionals are compliant. DECISION RULES: 1) Count lines: method is a few lines. 2) Look for loops/conditionals: none. 3) If short linear flow, mark compliant. VERDICT: compliant because the method is short and contains no loops or branching.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should comprehensively verify relevant properties of results. RATIONALE: Superficial assertions may pass while code is incorrect. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant tests verify multiple properties (2-3) or collection size and contents. DECISION RULES: 1) Count assertions: this test includes zero assertions. 2) If only a superficial or single assertion exists, mark non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because there are no assertions verifying properties of the constructed object; the test is unlikely to detect faults beyond constructor throwing an exception.

PRINCIPLE: Avoid ignored or commented-out tests; keep test code active. RATIONALE: Ignored tests provide no value and hide regressions. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Presence of @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out @Test marks non-compliant. DECISION RULES: 1) Search for @Ignore/@Disabled: not present on the method. 2) Search for commented-out @Test: not present. VERDICT: compliant because the test method is active (annotated with @Test) and not disabled or commented out.

PRINCIPLE: Each test should be traceable to a requirement or ticket. RATIONALE: Traceability aids impact analysis and coverage assessment. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for @Story/@Requirement annotations or Javadoc with IDs. DECISION RULES: 1) Search for traceability annotations or IDs in Javadoc: none present in the method. 2) If no traceability information, mark non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because there is no annotation or comment linking the test to any requirement or ticket.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Performance/security tests should be explicit and separate. RATIONALE: Non-functional requirements deserve dedicated tests. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Presence of timeout-based tests or explicit security tests marks compliance. DECISION RULES: 1) Unit tests are often not-applicable, but mark compliant if explicit performance/timeouts are present. 2) The method has @Test(timeout = 4000). VERDICT: compliant because the test uses a timeout annotation which is an explicit performance-related guard.

PRINCIPLE: Test names should describe scenario and expected outcome. RATIONALE: Descriptive names make tests self-documenting. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Names following methodName_scenario_expectedBehavior or test_when_then are compliant. DECISION RULES: 1) Check name: 'test9' is generic and does not describe scenario/outcome. 2) Generic names imply non-compliance. VERDICT: non-compliant because the method name 'test9' is not descriptive and does not reveal intent or expected behavior.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Auto-generated tests should be minimal and intention-revealing. RATIONALE: Verbose generated tests are hard to maintain. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for auto-generated comments or repetitive generic names (test0, test1, test9). DECISION RULES: 1) Search for auto-generated comments: none. 2) Search for repetitive/generic test names: method name 'test9' is a numeric generic name indicative of generated tests; the project imports EvoSuite classes (class-level) which suggests generation. 3) If evidence of heavy code generation patterns exists, mark non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because the method name is generic/numeric (test9) and there are clear signs of EvoSuite usage in the class, indicating auto-generation and a non-minimal generated footprint.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should show deliberate design (Given-When-Then or BDD naming). RATIONALE: Thoughtful design yields better coverage and maintainability. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Presence of Given-When-Then comments or BDD-style naming or multiple scenarios. DECISION RULES: 1) Look for Given-When-Then or BDD names: none. 2) If tests are minimal with only a basic happy path, mark non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because the single trivial test shows no evidence of prioritized or designed test cases (no BDD naming or structure).

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on public behavior and avoid reliance on implementation internals. RATIONALE: Behavior-focused tests are less brittle. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Tests using only public APIs without reflection are compliant. DECISION RULES: 1) Look for reflection usage: none. 2) If tests only call public methods or constructors and verify behavior, mark compliant. VERDICT: compliant because the test invokes the public constructor and does not use reflection or examine private internals.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should be specific and include messages where helpful. RATIONALE: Clear assertions improve failure diagnostics. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Assertions using assertEquals/assertThat with messages are preferred; generic assertTrue only is discouraged. DECISION RULES: 1) Count assertions with messages: this test has zero assertions. 2) If assertions are absent or only generic, mark non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because there are no assertions at all, so the test cannot detect or describe incorrect behavior.

PRINCIPLE: Comments should explain why, not what; avoid commented-out code. RATIONALE: Excessive or outdated comments are harmful. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant tests have minimal useful comments and no commented-out code. DECISION RULES: 1) Look for commented-out code: none in the method. 2) If code is clean with minimal comments, mark compliant. VERDICT: compliant because the method contains no commented-out code and is concise.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must be deterministic and avoid random/time-based behavior. RATIONALE: Deterministic tests prevent flakiness. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for Random(), current time, Thread.sleep(), external dependencies. DECISION RULES: 1) If none of these constructs appear and only local deterministic calls are present, mark compliant. VERDICT: compliant because the test only constructs an object and does not use randomness, time, sleeps, or external dependencies.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests must not leave persistent side effects or modify shared state. RATIONALE: Side effects cause inter-test coupling and flakiness. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant tests avoid file/db creation or static state modifications without cleanup. DECISION RULES: 1) Look for cleanup annotations or resource creation without cleanup: none. 2) If tests only use local variables and do not persist data, mark compliant. VERDICT: compliant because the test only creates a local object and does not interact with external systems or modify static/global state.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Use labels/categories (e.g., @Tag/@Category) to organize tests. RATIONALE: Enables selective execution of test subsets. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Presence of @Tag/@Category at class or method level is compliant. DECISION RULES: 1) Look for @Tag/@Category at class or method level: the class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), which applies to the method. 2) If meaningful labels are present, mark compliant. VERDICT: compliant because the class-level @Category(UnitTest.class) indicates the test is categorized.
